CONFIRM C0023 — The `action` property precedence gap for REJECTED-without-refutations is real. After C0002's fix ensures the `FindingFeedback` record is *created*, the record still gets `action="NONE"` because `self.refutations` is empty and no other field is populated by the builder's section 1. Traced execution: `build_feedback_records` section 1 creates the record when `final_v == "REJECTED"` and `refutations` is empty → `action` checks `self.refutations` (empty) → checks `self.admissibility_failures` (empty, not yet populated) → checks `self.duplicates` (empty) → checks `self.rk_discrepancy` (None) → returns `"NONE"`. A REJECTED finding with action NONE will not be flagged in the feedback prompt as needing corrective action. C0023's proposed fix (adding a `final_verdict == "REJECTED"` check to return `"RECALCULATE"`) is the simplest sufficient correction.

MERGE C0033 <- C0023 — Same root cause: `action` property doesn't account for `final_verdict="REJECTED"` as an independent trigger. C0033's description and fix target the same code path. C0023 has priority by filing order.

CONFIRM C0007 — The regex `(PASS|FAIL)` in `parse_admissibility_block` rejects any status that isn't exactly PASS or FAIL. If a model writes `N/A`, `SKIP`, or `PARTIAL`, the regex fails to match, `found_any` remains False, and the gate is counted as FAIL (missing). This is defensible for `N/A`/`SKIP` (treat as failure), but the current code conflates "gate reported non-PASS status" with "gate not reported at all" — both are counted as FAIL but for different reasons. The fix in C0024 (extending the regex to capture additional statuses and treating non-PASS as FAIL explicitly) is the correct approach for the PoC.

CONFIRM C0008 — The section_terminator regex is missing section headers that appear in actual model output (`FINDING_ID`, `NOVELTY`, etc. with `_ID` suffix patterns). C0020 and C0025 extend this with specific missing headers. DeepSeek's CHALLENGE argued that over-matching is worse than under-matching, but under-matching causes the admissibility block to consume text from subsequent sections, corrupting gate parsing. The risk of under-matching (wrong gate verdicts) exceeds the risk of over-matching (slightly smaller block to parse). CONFIRM the fix direction.

MERGE C0030 <- C0016 — Identical root cause: `build_feedback_records` section 3 only creates/updates a record for `fid_a`, never for `fid_b`. C0016 filed this first; C0030 and C0032 are independent rediscoveries.

MERGE C0032 <- C0016 — Same as above.

CONFIRM C0018 — `_rebuild_section` drops the full §17 instruction block (the 10-line directive about how to address each feedback type). When `max_chars_per_model` is exceeded and the while loop triggers a rebuild, models receive only "The schema has flagged the items below. Address each in this round." without the specific instructions for REFUTED/ADMISSIBILITY/DUPLICATE/R_k items. This silently degrades feedback quality under prompt pressure.

CONFIRM C0031 — The while loop `while len(section) > max_chars_per_model and len(top_items) > 1` stops at 1 item. If a single record's rendered text plus headers exceeds `max_chars_per_model`, the section silently exceeds the cap. The fix should add a final truncation or warning after the loop exits.
